claim.operational_target: Improve six-person later Senate Yea/Nay prequential NLL over a same-party dynamic relation control using a frozen party-relative person-item profile.
claim.interpretation: Success supports only party_relative_person_issue_predictive_utility in the frozen diagnostic scope.
alternatives: no stable person signal beyond party and recent history
same-party dynamic structure explains the gain
lexical or procedural repetition explains the gain
claim.scope: Six named incumbent U.S. Senators; Senate Yea/Nay roll calls; declared pre-choice Voteview text and metadata; Congress 116-119; final per-person windows frozen in experiment-manifest.json.

identifiability.distinguishing_evidence: A later non-overlapping temporal block compares the correct stable profile against the same-party dynamic model, a wrong same-party profile, and within-Congress shuffled fitting histories while all models update only after scoring.
unidentified_questions: Whether Voteview metadata was available before each vote
Whether a predictive profile represents reasons rather than strategy or coordination
Whether the relation transfers outside Senate roll calls

evidence.completeness_boundary: Local digests prove supplied bytes and role allocation only; source completeness, source timestamps, and pre-choice publication require an external archive or prospective registry.

computation.deployment_kernel: JointCoreModel.predict_probability plus run_prequential_state from the frozen work-only shared Logistic-normal kernel.
computation.selection_kernel: The identical reloaded JointCoreModel and prequential state kernel scored on Congress 118.
computation.uncertainty_scope: Laplace parameter covariance, scalar dynamic state variance, equal-person cluster bootstrap; excludes feature-map selection, model-family uncertainty, and source incompleteness.

results.summary: 1800 probabilities for six people recomputed from raw data and reloaded artifacts
229 production regression tests passed in 193.272 seconds

remaining_limitations: Source pre-choice availability is not externally proven
Semantic and causal interpretation remains unidentified
